$comment: Ratchet baseline for scripts/check/check-dependency-vulns.mjs. Keys are `<severity>:<package>` for findings reachable from a workspace runtime dependency set. Entries must be burned down, never added without a reason + reviewBy.

critical:@tarojs/components.reason: Advisory propagates from the swiper H5 implementation inside the Taro component package. WeChat builds compile to native <Swiper>, so this code path does not ship.

high:@tarojs/helper.reason: Same Taro build chain as above (helper is CLI-side only).

critical:@tarojs/taro.reason: Not an advisory of its own: npm audit marks @tarojs/taro critical because it depends on @tarojs/components (swiper H5 path) and @tarojs/helper (lodash). The only "fix" npm offers is downgrading Taro to 3.6.22, which breaks the mini-program build — permanently forbidden here. Separately from W2.3: swiper is now pinned back to 11.1.15 because @tarojs/components pins it exactly and the forced override did not resolve cleanly; real resolution lands with the Taro upgrade (W3).

high:braces.reason: Reached through Taro CLI globbing (chokidar/micromatch). Build-time only, no request path.

high:chokidar.reason: Taro CLI dev watcher; not present in the uploaded package.

high:find-yarn-workspace-root.reason: Taro CLI workspace detection utility; build-time only.

high:lodash.reason: No patched release exists (affected range is <=4.17.23, and 4.17.21 is current). Reachable only through build-time @tarojs/helper, which sits in the Taro runtime dependency list by framework convention; no app code imports lodash, and the three advisories only fire on _.template key names / _.unset / _.omit with attacker-controlled paths. Revisit when lodash ships a fix or with the Taro upgrade (W3).

high:micromatch.reason: Taro CLI glob matching; build-time only.

critical:swiper.reason: Prototype pollution in swiper <12.1.2, reachable only through @tarojs/components H5 output. apps/mini-program/src has zero swiper imports and WeChat uses the native <Swiper>. npm audit fix would downgrade @tarojs/* to 3.2.16, which breaks the build.
